title: regional-latency-aware-margin-waterfall-workbook
content:
Purpose:
This workbook decomposes Hosted API unit economics by region and by latency bucket to reveal where marginal latency and caching improvements translate to dollar savings. It's an intentionally compact, scenario-driven sheet for alignment with Eng + Product on near-term optimizations (batching knobs, kv-cache heatmaps, model routing).

Status / how to use:
- Draft: numbers are best-effort from Q4 infra meter + cloud invoices.
- Cells marked with [EST] are estimated from invoice-topology mapping.
- Use the scenario table at the end to swap cache hit / batching / p50 latency targets.

Assumptions (high level):
- GPU token cost mapped by model family (v1/v2): cost_per_gpu_token = GPU_hourly_cost / (tokens_per_second * 3600) adjusted for utilization.
- Infra overhead = load-balancer + control-plane + regional infra amortization (15% base across regions; configurable).
- Network egress priced per GB; avg token => 4 bytes/token (text-only) for rough egress calc.
- KV cache reduces generation token count (post-prompt) by cache_hit_rate * avg_cached_prefix_tokens.
- Batching reduces GPU time per request but increases tail latency; we model conservative concurrency-friendly batching.

Quick spreadsheet extract (representative rows):

Columns: Model, Region, p50_ms, p95_ms, avg_req_tokens, gen_tokens_after_cache, gpu_token_cost_usd, infra_overhead_usd, egress_usd, total_cogs_per_req_usd, price_per_req_usd, margin_usd, margin_pct

Rows (sample):
- gptx-small, us-west, 85, 210, 420, 300, $0.00034, $0.00005, $0.00002, $0.00041, $0.00120, $0.00079, 65.8%
- gptx-small, eu-west, 92, 240, 420, 300, $0.00038, $0.00006, $0.00003, $0.00047, $0.00140, $0.00093, 66.4%
- gptx-medium, us-west, 120, 420, 1200, 900, $0.00102, $0.00012, $0.00006, $0.00120, $0.00350, $0.00230, 65.7%
- gptx-large, us-west, 220, 900, 1600, 1500, $0.00275, $0.00018, $0.00008, $0.00301, $0.00700, $0.00399, 57.0%

Notes on decomposition:
- gpu_token_cost_usd = gen_tokens_after_cache * per_token_rate_by_model_region.
- infra_overhead_usd = per-request amortization of control-plane + LB + autoscaling buffer. (We currently hardcode a 15% uplift on top of GPU cost at region-level; this is likely overstated for high-concurrency customers.)
- egress_usd = (avg_req_tokens * bytes_per_token) / (1024^3) * egress_rate_by_region.

Sensitivity slices included in sheet:
1) KV-cache hit rate: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% (affects gen_tokens_after_cache).
2) Batching efficiency: none, conservative (10% token-time reduction), aggressive (25%).
3) Regional price deltas: on-prem-equivalent, us-west priced baseline, eu-west +6%, ap-southeast +12%.
4) Tail-latency penalty: model routing fallbacks to cheaper model if p95 > threshold.

Scenario matrix (extracted):
- Base (current): kv_hit=30%, batching=10% => net per-1M-req savings vs 0% cache/0% batching: $650
- Optimistic: kv_hit=60%, batching=25% => net per-1M-req savings: $1,880 (heavy benefit on large models where gen tokens dominate)
- Pessimistic: kv_hit=10%, batching=0% => net per-1M-req savings: $210

Regional callouts (observed):
- EU regions show ~8–10% higher infra+egress COGS vs US due to both egress and smaller instance price parity; margin impact concentrated on small models where per-request overhead matters.
- APAC shows highest delta in egress but lower GPU list-rate discounts for burst capacity; opportunity: route inference for long-form completions to regional cheaper pools when latency SLO allows.

Waterfall visualization (textual) per model-region (example, gptx-medium / us-west):
- Gross revenue per req: $0.00350
- - GPU raw token cost: $0.00102
- - Infra overhead: $0.00012
- - Egress: $0.00006
- - Payment processing & entitlements: $0.00005 [EST]
= Contribution margin: $0.00225 (64.3%)
- - Fixed reserved capacity amortization (if on Dedicated routing): $0.00030
= Net margin after reserved amortization: $0.00195 (55.7%)

Actionable optimization levers (ranked):
1) KV-cache: prioritize feature/traces for long-tail prefixes. Impact: largest for large-context models and high repetition workloads. Quick wins: 25% uplift in hit rate by improving prefix normalization and TTL heuristics.
2) Dynamic batching policy by model/route: enable conservative batching on medium-compute families for background workloads. Impact: high on throughput customers; tradeoff: increased p95 for chat/interactive.
3) Regional model routing: route low-SLO workloads (async summarization) to ap-southeast cheaper pool during off-peak windows. Requires: per-customer policy and transparent pricing.
4) Tail-aware fallback: automatically route to smaller quantized variant on p95 exceed; measure quality delta with eval prompts before rollout.

Low-effort experiments to run (2–6 weeks):
- Experiment A (KV quickplay): roll improved prefix normalization for 10% of traffic on gptx-medium; measure change in gen_tokens_after_cache and latency.
- Experiment B (Batching gate): enable 10–20ms extra batching window for long-form endpoints behind a feature flag; measure tokens/sec uplift and p95 shift.
- Experiment C (Regional routing pilot): pilot routing 5% of async traffic from EU to APAC cheaper pool with simulated SLOs and telemetry for error/latency.

Open questions / data needs:
- We need per-customer per-route utilization histograms (seq length distribution) to better size batching policies. Current histogram is coarse. (Jira: ENG-4123)
- Confirm whether infra overhead should be amortized as percent-of-GPU-cost or as fixed per-request (SRE input).
- Precise bytes/token for multimodal workloads — current 4 bytes/token understates image/embedding outputs.

Risks / quality considerations:
- Aggressive batching reduces unit costs but can cause SLA breaches for interactive applications; must be gated by route-level SLO and blackbox canary.
- KV cache correctness: false hits (stale or wrong prefix mapping) cause hallucination risk. Need eval suite.

Recommendation summary (short):
- Prioritize KV cache normalization and TTL changes (owner: Product + Applied ML) — highest immediate $/1M benefit.
- Add a conservative batching policy experiment for background-only routes (owner: Serving Runtime + SRE).
- Build a small cross-region routing pilot for bulk async workloads, instrument egress and latencies.

Next steps / owners:
- Product-optimize to own experiment design + KPI deck (Ellen Rivera) — due 2026-03-05
- Applied-ML to produce kv-cache hit-rate simulation v2 (Rohan Gupta) — due 2026-02-28
- Serving-runtime to scope batching feature flag and metrics (Marco DeLuca) — due 2026-03-10

Appendix (calcs and example formulas):
- per_token_gpu_cost = model_rate_by_region ($/M tokens) / 1_000_000
- total_cogs = gen_tokens_after_cache * per_token_gpu_cost + infra_overhead + egress + payment_fees
- margin_per_req = price_per_req - total_cogs

Raw numbers and full pivot tables live in the linked Confluence sandbox and the Optimize GitHub workbook (see linked_artifacts).

Notes to self (informal):
- Double-check ap-southeast list-rate for rtx-8000 equivalent; billing mapping fuzzy when burst capacity applied.
- Consider adding embedding-only route slice (very different token:byte ratio, different egress profile).
- Keep sheet minimal — stakeholders prefer 1-page executive table + 2 scenario tabs.

-- end of draft workbook export --
